stories.headline: Amazon Invests Up to $25B in Anthropic, Secures $100B+ AWS Compute Commitment Over 10 Years

key_facts.fact: Amazon will invest $5 billion in Anthropic immediately, with up to $20 billion more tied to commercial milestones, on top of $8 billion already invested — bringing total potential investment to ~$33 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon to invest $5 billion in Anthropic today and up to an additional $20 billion in the future. This is in addition to the $8 billion Amazon previously invested in Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic commits to spending more than $100 billion on AWS technologies over the next 10 years, including current and future generations of Trainium chips (Trainium2 through Trainium4) and tens of millions of Graviton CPU cores.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic to spend more than $100 billion over the next ten years on AWS technologies. This encompasses current and future generations of Trainium and tens of millions of Graviton cores.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic secures up to 5 gigawatts of compute capacity, with nearly 1 GW of combined Trainium2 and Trainium3 capacity expected online by end of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic secures up to 5 gigawatts of capacity to train and deploy its Claude models under the deal. Amazon said that significant Trainium2 capacity is coming online in the second quarter of 2026, with nearly one gigawatt of combined Trainium2 and Trainium3 expected by year-end.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's annualized revenue has reached $30 billion, up from approximately $9 billion at end of 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: the company's annualised revenue has reached $30 billion, up from approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025.

key_facts.fact: The initial investment is priced at Anthropic's latest valuation of $380 billion. Over 100,000 customers run Claude models on AWS.
key_facts.excerpt: over 100,000 customers run Anthropic Claude models on AWS, making Claude one of the most popular model families on Amazon Bedrock.

key_facts.fact: The deal follows Amazon's $50 billion investment in OpenAI announced two months earlier, making Amazon the largest investor in both leading AI labs.
key_facts.excerpt: The new investment in Anthropic, the creator of Claude, follows Amazon's announcement earlier this year it would invest up to $50 billion in OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT.

stories.headline: Moonshot AI Releases Kimi K2.6, Open-Weight 1T-Parameter Model Rivaling Frontier Labs on Coding

key_facts.fact: Kimi K2.6 is a 1 trillion total parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 32 billion active parameters per token, 384 experts (8 routed + 1 shared), 256K context window, and native multimodal input (text, image, video).
key_facts.excerpt: a Mixture-of-Experts system with 1 trillion total parameters and 32 billion active per token. It ships with open weights on Hugging Face under a Modified MIT license, native INT4 quantization, and a 256K context window

key_facts.fact: K2.6 scores 80.2% on SWE-Bench Verified, 58.6% on SWE-Bench Pro (beating Claude Opus 4.6's 53.4% and GPT-5.4's 57.7%), and 54.0% on Humanity's Last Exam with tools (beating GPT-5.4's 52.1%).
key_facts.excerpt: SWE-Bench Verified 80.2%, SWE-Bench Pro 58.6% vs Claude Opus 4.6 53.4%, Humanity's Last Exam (with tools) 54.0% vs GPT-5.4 52.1%

key_facts.fact: The model supports an agent-swarm primitive coordinating up to 300 parallel sub-agents across 4,000 steps per run, and can code continuously for 12+ hours.
key_facts.excerpt: 300 parallel sub-agents, 12-hour autonomous coding sessions

key_facts.fact: K2.6 ranks #4 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0, scoring 54 — just 3 points behind Claude Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.4, all tied at 57.
key_facts.excerpt: Kimi K2.6 has debuted at #4 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0, scoring 54 out of a possible index points — just three points behind the trio of Anthropic (Claude Opus 4.7), Google (Gemini 3.1 Pro), and OpenAI (GPT-5.4), all of which are tied at 57.

key_facts.fact: API pricing is $0.60 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens — roughly 10× cheaper than Claude Opus 4.7. Weights available on Hugging Face under Modified MIT License.
key_facts.excerpt: priced at $0.60 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens through the Kimi API. Claude Opus 4.7 lists at $5 and $25 for the same surfaces.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches Chronicle for Codex, Building AI Memory From Screen Captures

key_facts.fact: Chronicle is a research preview feature in Codex for macOS that periodically captures screenshots, sends them to OpenAI servers for processing, and stores text summaries as local unencrypted Markdown files to build persistent context.
key_facts.excerpt: Chronicle periodically captures your screen, processes the content into text summaries, and stores those summaries as local memory files that give the AI assistant context about what you have been working on.

key_facts.fact: Available only to ChatGPT Pro subscribers ($100+/month) on Apple Silicon Macs. Not available in the EU, UK, or Switzerland. Requires macOS Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions.
key_facts.excerpt: Chronicle is in an opt-in research preview. It is only available for ChatGPT Pro subscribers on macOS, and is not yet available in the EU, UK and Switzerland.

key_facts.fact: Screen captures are stored temporarily on-device and auto-deleted after 6 hours. OpenAI says screenshots are not stored on servers after processing and are not used for training.
key_facts.excerpt: Screen captures are ephemeral and will only be saved temporarily on your computer. Screen captures that are older than 6 hours will be deleted while Chronicle is running.

key_facts.fact: Chronicle processes screenshots in the cloud, contrasting with Microsoft Recall's on-device approach and drawing comparisons to the now-defunct Rewind AI. OpenAI warns the feature increases risk of prompt injection from screen content.
key_facts.excerpt: Recall takes screenshots and processes them locally using the neural processing unit on the device. No screenshot data leaves the machine. Chronicle takes the opposite approach: processing happens in the cloud.

key_facts.fact: Over one million developers have used Codex, and usage doubled following the GPT-5.2-Codex model launch in December. Chronicle is part of a broader update that added computer use, in-app browser, image generation, and 90+ plugins.
key_facts.excerpt: Over one million developers have used Codex, and usage doubled following the launch of the GPT-5.2-Codex model in December.

stories.headline: GitHub Copilot Pauses New Signups, Tightens Limits, and Removes Opus Models From Pro Tier

key_facts.fact: GitHub paused new sign-ups for Copilot Pro, Pro+, and Student plans on April 20, citing agentic workflows that 'fundamentally changed Copilot's compute demands.'
key_facts.excerpt: New sign-ups are paused for GitHub Copilot Pro, Pro+, and Student plans. GitHub states this allows them to serve existing customers more effectively.

key_facts.fact: Opus models removed from Pro plans entirely; Opus 4.7 remains available on Pro+ only. Opus 4.5 and 4.6 being removed from Pro+ as previously announced.
key_facts.excerpt: Opus models are no longer available in Pro plans. Opus 4.7 remains available in Pro+ plans. As we announced in our changelog, Opus 4.5 and Opus 4.6 will be removed from Pro+.

key_facts.fact: Usage limits tightened for individual plans, with Pro+ now offering more than 5× the limits of Pro. Two types of limits: session limits (prevent peak overload) and weekly token-consumption caps.
key_facts.excerpt: Usage limits are being tightened for individual plans. Pro+ plans now offer more than 5X the limits of Pro plans.

key_facts.fact: GitHub is offering refunds for Pro or Pro+ subscriptions canceled between April 20 and May 20, 2026, acknowledging the changes are disruptive.
key_facts.excerpt: GitHub acknowledges these changes are disruptive and is offering refunds for Pro or Pro+ subscriptions canceled between April 20 and May 20, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Long-running, parallelized agentic sessions now consume far more resources than the original plan structure was built to support, GitHub VP of product Joe Binder said.
key_facts.excerpt: Agentic workflows have fundamentally changed Copilot's compute demands. Long-running, parallelized sessions now regularly consume far more resources than the original plan structure was built to support.

stories.headline: Trump Says DOD Deal With Anthropic 'Possible' After White House Meeting With Amodei

key_facts.fact: President Trump told CNBC on April 21 that 'it's possible' a deal will be made to allow Anthropic to resume contracting with the Department of Defense, describing last week's White House meeting as 'very good talks.'
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump on Tuesday told CNBC that 'it's possible' that a deal will be made to allow Anthropic's... He described Amodei's meeting with Wiles as 'very good'

key_facts.fact: The statement follows Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's meeting last Friday with White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, described by both sides as 'productive and constructive.'
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei walked into the West Wing for a meeting with White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was also in the room. The White House called the talks 'productive and constructive.'

key_facts.fact: The reversal is striking: weeks ago the Trump administration had declared Anthropic a supply chain risk — a designation reserved for foreign adversaries — and Trump said the administration would 'not do business with them again.'
key_facts.excerpt: Just weeks ago, the Trump administration had declared Anthropic a supply chain risk – a designation ordinarily reserved for foreign adversaries – and Trump himself said the administration would 'not do business with them again.'

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's Mythos AI cybersecurity capability is what changed the calculus — civilian agencies and intelligence agencies want access to Mythos's vulnerability-discovery capabilities and are unwilling to be locked out by the Pentagon dispute.
key_facts.excerpt: What changed the calculus – at least at the White House level – was Anthropic Mythos AI cybersecurity ability. Specifically, the fact that agencies are purportedly watching Mythos do things no other tool can, and are not willing to sit that out.

stories.headline: Bezos' Project Prometheus Nears $10B Fundraise at $38B Valuation for Industrial AI

key_facts.fact: Jeff Bezos' AI startup Project Prometheus is close to finalizing a $10 billion funding round at a $38 billion post-money valuation, according to the Financial Times.
key_facts.excerpt: Jeff Bezos is close to finalizing a $10 billion funding round for his AI startup that's developing models with the capability of understanding the physical world, the Financial Times reported. The fresh funding values the company, code-named Project Prometheus, at $38 billion.

key_facts.fact: JPMorgan and BlackRock are among the investors in the new round. The startup was initially set up with $6.2 billion in funding, sourced in part from Bezos himself.
key_facts.excerpt: JPMorgan and BlackRock are among the investors in the new round, the FT said. The startup was set up with an initial $6.2 billion in funding, sourced in part from Bezos himself.

key_facts.fact: Project Prometheus, co-founded by Bezos and scientist Vik Bajaj, focuses on AI models for the physical world — accelerating engineering and manufacturing in aerospace, automobiles, and semiconductors.
key_facts.excerpt: Project Prometheus, which Bezos co-founded with scientist Vik Bajaj, will use AI to accelerate engineering and manufacturing in fields like aerospace and automobiles. The company aims to bring innovation to sectors such as manufacturing, aerospace, and semiconductors.

key_facts.fact: The startup has recruited dozens of employees from leading AI labs including OpenAI and Google DeepMind, in San Francisco, Zurich, and London.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup has dozens of employees, some of whom were poached from leading AI labs like OpenAI and Google DeepMind, and it has been recruiting AI talent in San Francisco, Zurich and London.

stories.headline: Google's Sergey Brin Forms DeepMind 'Coding Strike Team' to Close Gap With Anthropic

key_facts.fact: Google co-founder Sergey Brin is personally leading a new DeepMind 'Coding Strike Team' aimed at closing Gemini's gap with Anthropic's Claude on code generation, according to The Information.
key_facts.excerpt: Google co-founder Sergey Brin has reportedly urged DeepMind employees to focus on improving AI agents... Google assembles a dedicated team of researchers and engineers to strengthen its AI coding models.

key_facts.fact: In an internal memo, Brin wrote: 'To win the final sprint, we must urgently bridge the gap in agentic execution and turn our models into primary developers.' He framed improving coding as the path to self-improving AI — AI that trains the next AI.
key_facts.excerpt: In the memo, Brin wrote, 'To win the final sprint, we must urgently bridge the gap in agentic execution and turn our models into primary developers' of code. The end goal is AI takeoff, or AI that can improve itself.

key_facts.fact: The strike team is led by research engineer Sebastian Borgeaud, who previously ran DeepMind's pretraining. Both Brin and DeepMind CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu are directly involved.
key_facts.excerpt: Research engineer Sebastian Borgeaud, who previously ran DeepMind's pretraining, is leading the group under CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu and Brin.

key_facts.fact: DeepMind researchers internally rate Claude's code-writing above Gemini's, which drove Brin's push. Google is now training models on its own proprietary codebase rather than public datasets typically used for general-purpose coding agents.
key_facts.excerpt: Researchers at Google DeepMind view Anthropic's coding tools as ahead of the code-writing capabilities of Google's Gemini models. Google is now placing more emphasis on models that write code for internal use, shifting from its earlier focus on tools for external customers.

key_facts.fact: Gemini engineers are now required to use Google's internal agent tools on complex tasks, with usage tracked on a company leaderboard called 'Jetski.'
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini engineers now have to use Google's internal agent tools on complex tasks, with usage tracked on a company leaderboard called Jetski.
